newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes firmer, Dec Oman trades at premium.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes firmer, Dec Oman trades at premium.

text.p: Crude oil prices were firmer in Asia on Wednesday with Brent futures spurred higher to fresh five year highs towards the expiry of the November contract.

Tight distillate stocks in the U.S., reported overnight by the American Petroleum Institute and buying by a European major was enough to push November to a post Gulf War high of $25.15 on SIMEX, surpassing the previous Brent high of $25.06 hit in London on Tuesday. The November futures contract expires later on Wednesday.
The European major paid 55 cents for a Nov/Dec Brent cash spread from a Wall Street trader, bolstering November prices.
The spread had gone out in New York Tuesday at 44/47 cents. The major was also bidding for partial December Brent cargoes.
Dubai intermonth spreads were steady, valued around 52 cents for near months, while paper Tapis was quiet. December was bid at $24.70, about five cents up on the day earlier.
The wider Brent spreads tightened up the Brent/Dubai slightly to $2.45/$2.55 for December from a day-earlier $2.35/$2.55.

In the wet market, December Oman barrels were underway with a trader -- which placed October and November barrels quite late -- exchanging a cargo to a European major at MPM plus four cents, traders said.
Another December cargo changed hands at MPM plus five, although details were vague, traders said. A million barrels of November traded into South Africa at dated Brent less $1.80.
A November Oman cargo traded at MPM less seven cents per barrel between a trader and a U.S. major, which finally placed all the November Oman crude, traders said.
